evidence.E1: The split is structural, not commentary: `WebhookApp` (src/webhookd/app.py:141) does route/verify/freshness/record and returns; `Worker` (src/webhookd/worker.py:65) is a separate class with its own thread pool, lease, backoff and dead-letter policy; `Service` (app.py:504) wires them and `create_app` takes `start_worker` so a caller can get the WSGI callable without spawning threads (app.py:561-574). `--no-worker` on `webhookd serve` and a standalone `webhookd worker` command make the two halves independently deployable (`webhookd serve --help` output). README.md:63 documents the ordering diagram and README.md 'Handler execution is at-least-once' (line 221) states the consequence the design accepts.

unanticipated_findings: Dedup identity is not covered by the signature, so idempotency can be defeated inside the tolerance window by mutating one unsigned header. The default scheme template is `{timestamp}.{body}` (src/webhookd/config.py:52) and the default dedup strategy is `header_or_digest` keyed on `X-Webhook-Delivery` (config.py:69-70), which the HMAC does not cover. Reproduced against a live server: POST a correctly signed body with `X-Webhook-Delivery: evt-1` -> 202 delivery_id 1; replay the identical bytes and identical signature with `X-Webhook-Delivery: evt-1-TAMPERED` -> 202 delivery_id 3, and the handler wrote a second file (var/events/acme/2026-08-07/000000000001-h_evt-1.json AND 000000000003-h_evt-1-TAMPERED.json). Any party that can observe and re-send a delivery within `tolerance_seconds` (default 300) gets duplicate downstream work — the exact outcome the design exists to prevent. Setting `dedup_strategy = "digest"` closes it, but that is not the default and the README does not flag the trade-off.

A timestamp of `nan` silently disables the replay window. src/webhookd/signatures.py:209-213 parses the `unix` format with bare `float(raw)`, which accepts "nan"/"NaN"; src/webhookd/app.py:349 then evaluates `abs(skew) > sender.tolerance_seconds`, and any comparison against NaN is False, so the freshness check passes. Reproduced live: a request signed over timestamp "nan" returned `202 {"delivery_id": 3, "duplicate": false}` and the NaN was persisted to the `event_timestamp` column, while "inf", "-inf" and "1e999" were all correctly rejected with 400. Exploiting it requires a valid signature over the literal "nan", so it is not an unauthenticated bypass, but it is an unguarded hole in the one check that bounds replay, and no test covers it (tests/test_signatures.py:266 test_parse_timestamp_rejects_junk does not include nan/inf).

`/stats` is exposed without authentication by default. src/webhookd/config.py:123-124 defaults `expose_stats = True` and `stats_token = ""`, and src/webhookd/app.py:252 only enforces the bearer token `if self.config.stats_token`. The config `webhookd init` writes sets `stats_token = "${WEBHOOKD_STATS_TOKEN:-}"`, which resolves to empty unless the operator knows to set it. Reproduced: `curl http://127.0.0.1:8391/stats` with no credentials returned `{"backlog": 0, "by_sender": {"acme": 3}, "by_status": {...}, "newest_received_at": 1786097281.56, "oldest_received_at": ..., "total": 3, "uptime_seconds": 70.3}` — per-sender delivery volumes and timing, which is business-sensitive on a host that terminates public webhooks. `webhookd check` does print a warning about it, so this is an insecure default rather than a hidden one.

Minor: `delivery_id` values in responses are not contiguous because SQLite's AUTOINCREMENT consumes a rowid on the `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` path (src/webhookd/store.py:49 + :323). In the reproduction above the second accepted delivery was reported as `delivery_id: 3`, not 2. Harmless for correctness — dedup is on the UNIQUE constraint, not the id — but the ids are documented in README.md:187 'The event' as the stable handler-side idempotency key and a reader may reasonably expect them to be dense.
